newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan '97 auto exports won't rise despite yen - JAMA.
newsitem.headline: Japan '97 auto exports won't rise despite yen - JAMA.

text.p: Japan's vehicle exports are unlikely to rise in 1997 despite the weaker yen, Yoshifumi Tsuji, chairman of the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association (JAMA), told a news conference on Thursday.
"Exports of built-up vehicles will keep falling regardless of the movements in currencies, and they will be replaced by locally produced vehicles," he said.
In late January, Andrew Card, president of the American Automobile Manufacturers Association, said the yen's excessive depreciation threatened to reignite trade friction with the United States.

On Wednesday, Richard Wagoner, president of General Motors North American Operations, said the U.S. market share gains by Toyota and other Japanese automakers in January were due in large measure to the sharp fall in the yen.

"Japan's exports to the United States rose only 0.3 percent between April 1996 and January 1997, not a drastic increase. Exports of European cars to the United States gained 16 percent. Japanese car imports are not a threat to American makers," he said.
